tob-0035: Lately opened files tell of Stargate — the CIA and Army’s twenty-year try at spying by mind-power. Far-seers strove to find hostages, submarines, and secret works by thought alone. The papers show what the government learned, and why the program was at last shut down.
tob-4135: A. E. Waite’s huge Kabalah book surveys its teachings, its growth, and its writings — the Zohar above all. Wrought with his wonted deep learning, it was the English wonder-seeker’s bible on the theme. The book stays a landmark of Kabbalah scholarship.
tob-4235: William Smith’s olden-world wordbook — 1842 — is the great Victorian handbook of Greek and Roman life, law, worship, and war. Learned men penned its deep articles. Generations of schoolboys learned antiquity from its pages. The work stays a monument of classic book-lore.
tob-13335: Evelyn Underhill’s Inwardness — 1911 — is the classic English sifting of the holy life, from Plotinus to Teresa and John of the Cross. Her great muster made soul-science open to all. The book stays the standard door to inwardness.
tob-14435: Sextus’s Sayings — from the Nag Hammadi hoard — string near five hundred wise-man’s saws on the wise and holy life, half Pythagoras, half Christ. These short sayings steered monks and thinkers alike. The work is a gem of olden wisdom letters.
cia-0000112335: An August 1990 report on an airship-like UFO sighted over Murmansk, the Soviet Arctic naval base. Strange lights over a top-secret fleet headquarters would interest any intelligence service — whatever they turned out to be. The entry shows Cold War spying had room for the unexplained, filed right alongside the missiles.
cia-0000112835: An estimated October 1945 list of collaborators in the Shanghai area. After Japan's surrender, settling accounts with those who had cooperated with the occupiers was urgent business. The document names names — the postwar reckoning, reduced to a list.
cia-0000119735: A September 1956 survey of Hungary's present political situation — the calm, or the tension, before the October storm. Analysts mapped the factions, the grievances, and the pressure building inside the party. The document reads now like a weather report filed just before the hurricane.
cia-0000124335: A September 1958 report on a Moscow industrial and agricultural exhibit — including models of Sputniks and electronics equipment. The Soviets showed off their satellites like trophies at a fair. The CIA studied the exhibits too: even propaganda models revealed engineering truths.
cia-0000132235: Situation Report 552: Iran's foreign minister Velayati to hold talks — the truncated title cuts off with whom. Tehran was maneuvering around the war next door, seeking advantage. The document watches Iran play its careful game: enemy of Iraq, wary of America.
cia-0000132635: Item 14 in the June 1960 series: Cuba postponing its underdeveloped nations conference indefinitely. The grand Third World summit was shelved — ambition meeting reality. The document is the postponement: the conference, deferred.
cia-0000135835: A situation report on PBSUCCESS for April 20 to 26, 1954 — the coup's final countdown, week by week. The invasion was days away. The document is the countdown: the week, reported — the zero hour, near.
cia-0000135935: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN reporting the need for fabricated operational documents. Forgeries were tools of the trade — fake papers for real operations. The document is the admission: the fakes, required.
cia-0000136135: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for ONTRICH with SKILLET information on a possible arms shipment — and instructions, the truncated title suggests. The guns, tracked. The document is the shipment: the arms, watched.
cia-0000136335: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN providing a summary of RO material received from the 0800 report — the truncated title cuts off the date. The morning's take. The entry is the summary: the material, provided.
cia-0000136935: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN on leaflet drops. The paper war, again. The document is the drop: the leaflets, scattered.
cia-0000137335: The record of the 401st NSC briefing on Thursday, April 23, 1959, with an attached document — the truncated title cuts off the subject. The April briefing. The document is the session: the 401st, held.
cia-0000139035: A 1946 military information report on a Soviet-Mongolian military mission to Kalgan — the archive's spelling says soveit. The mission, noted. The entry is the visit: the delegation, tracked — through a typo.
cia-0000139135: A Middle East area brief — subject deleted — for August 30, 1990. The region on the eve of the Gulf War. The document is the brief: the eve, covered — the subject, hidden.
cia-0000141135: An estimated 1976 text of a conversation between Thorsrud and Pfeiffer. The talk, transcribed. The document is the dialogue: the speakers, recorded.
un-ga-res-35: General Assembly Resolution 35, adopted in 1946. The Assembly's first year produced the grammar of modern multilateralism. This resolution is one sentence in that grammar — the catalog gives the number, the text gives the words.
un-ga-res-a-69-35: General Assembly Resolution A/69/35, adopted in 2014. The session rolled on. The entry is the record: the thirty-fifth, preserved.
un-sc-res-135: Security Council Resolution 135, adopted in 1960. The young decade's Council deciding. The designation and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-235: Security Council Resolution 235, adopted in 1967. The Six-Day War year's Council. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1035: Security Council Resolution 1035, adopted in December 1995 — the resolution creating the UN Mission in Bosnia and Herzegovina, including the international police task force. After Dayton, the Council sent police instead of soldiers. The resolution is the mission: the law, rebuilt.
un-sc-res-1335: Security Council Resolution 1335, cataloged with the year 1999 — the numbering suggests 2001, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1835: Security Council Resolution 1835, adopted in September 2008 — the Iran resolution, reaffirming the demand that Tehran suspend enrichment and comply with the IAEA. The nuclear standoff's diplomatic drumbeat continued. The resolution is the reaffirmation: the demand, repeated.
un-sc-res-2735: Security Council Resolution 2735, adopted in June 2024 — the Gaza ceasefire resolution, endorsing the three-phase ceasefire proposal for the Israel-Hamas war. The Council backed the American plan. The resolution is the endorsement: the ceasefire, proposed.
plos-pone-0000035: A 2006 PLOS ONE study on the restructuring of pancreatic islets and insulin secretion in a postnatal — the truncated title cuts off the model. The insulin-making clusters of the pancreas, remodeled after birth. The paper is the restructuring: the islets, reshaped.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d35: President Roosevelt to Marshal Stalin, October 4, 1943 — Document 35. October opened with a letter to Moscow. The message is the opening: the month, begun.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d135: A memorandum by the first secretary of the embassy in the Soviet Union, Bohlen — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 135. Moscow embassy thinking, on paper. The memo is the thinking: Bohlen, recording.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d235: A paper prepared by the Joint Staff Planners, November 14, 1943 — Document 235. The planners' product, filed late. The paper is the product: the planners, preparing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d335: The Assistant Secretary of War McCloy to the Secretary of War Stimson — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 335. The number two wrote number one. The memo is the internal: McCloy, to Stimson.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d435: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 435. The editors' bridge. The note is the bridge: the narrative, connected.
philip-dru-administrator-a-story-of-tomo: Written anonymously by Colonel Edward House — President Wilson's closest adviser — this political novel imagines a benevolent strongman remaking America. Philip Dru seizes power to enact sweeping reforms, from banking to labor laws. Part utopia, part warning, it is a fascinating glimpse into progressive-era dreams of government.
adventures-of-huckleberry-finn-chapters-: Huck's crisis of conscience — shall he free Jim or turn him in? — reaches its peak here, in the famous passage where he chooses to go to hell for his friend. Tom Sawyer's arrival then turns rescue into boyish farce. The moral heart of the novel.
arxiv-2605-08935: Weather, traffic, and epidemics all evolve across space and time together — coupled spatiotemporal forecasting. Hao Wu, Fan Xu, Yuxu Lu, and colleagues propose PnP-Corrector, a universal plug-and-play framework that corrects such forecasts after the fact. The 2026 paper is about fixing predictions, whatever model made them.
arxiv-2605-09435: Parikh images count letter occurrences while forgetting their order; star complexity measures how hard those images are to describe. Yoav Danieli studies both for languages over infinite alphabets, where the usual finite tricks fail. The 2026 paper is automata theory on counting abstractions.
arxiv-2605-09535: The Erdős–Kleitman problem asks how large a family of subsets can be without containing a matching of a given size. Cheng Chi and Yan Wang approach it through the lens of the Erdős matching conjecture. The 2026 paper is extremal combinatorics on a classic problem.
arxiv-2605-10135: Large-scale approximate nearest neighbor indexing accelerated by cost-effective cloud GPUs — ScaleGANN. Lan Lu, Peiqi Yin, Isaac Yang, and colleagues build the system. The 2026 paper is vector search at cloud scale. It indexes massively and affordably at once.
plos-pone-0003435: Cardiologists followed Chinese adults for years in this 2008 study to test an artery measurement. Thicker inner walls of the carotid artery, and the presence of plaque, turned out to predict future heart disease and stroke. The prospective evidence supports using a simple neck ultrasound to flag people at risk before symptoms appear.
plos-pone-0003535: Cancer researchers built a new window into bone pain in this 2008 paper. Prostate tumors that spread to bone cause excruciating pain, and their mouse xenograft model showed the alpha 6 integrin, a cell-grip protein, drives both migration and suffering. The model gives drug hunters a living system for testing pain relief alongside tumor control.
plos-pone-0003635: Neuroscientists Katoh, Chapman, and Raymond found motor timing unlearnable without a calcium channel in this 2008 study. Mice lacking P/Q-type calcium channels could not adjust the timing of their movements through practice. The result pins learned timing, the fine temporal tuning of motion, to a specific molecular channel.
plos-pone-0003735: In 2008, Dubin-Thaler, Hofman, and Cai clocked the engines of crawling cells. Measuring edge speeds and the pulling forces of moving cells, they found distinct motility modules at work. The force maps break cell crawling into parts, with uses from immune defense to stopping cancer spread.
plos-pone-0003835: A 2008 neuroscience study found the brain's birth rate keeps daily time. Adult neurogenesis in the hippocampus, the birth of new neurons in grown brains, rose and fell with the time of day. The rhythm suggests the brain schedules its own renewal by the clock.
plos-pone-0003935: In 2008, Kempa, Krasensky, and Dal Santo put a plant hormone at metabolism's center. Abscisic acid, the drought-and-stress signal, was found directing carbohydrate metabolism under duress. The hormone's central role links environmental hardship to sugar management. The finding explains how stressed plants ration their energy.
plos-pone-0004035: In 2008, Rubinoff and Le Roux found moths evolving in leaps, not steps. The sphinx moth genus Proserpinus showed repeated, independent bursts of rapid change. Such saltational evolution is rarely invoked by biologists, yet here it happened twice. The peculiar moth genus becomes a showcase for evolution's sudden jumps.
plos-pone-0004135: In 2009, Leong, Zhou, and Lim found a fat tag building bone. Protein palmitoylation steered osteoblast differentiation through osterix. The fatty modification switched on bone-forming programs. The switch names a target for osteoporosis drugs. Blocking or boosting the tag could tune bone growth.
plos-pone-0004235: In 2009, Mahller, Williams, and Baird hunted neuroblastoma's roots. Neuroblastoma cell lines harbored pluripotent tumor-initiating cells within. The rare cells resisted standard therapy stubbornly. A targeted oncolytic virus killed them cleanly. The finding aims treatment at the true source at last.
plos-pone-0004335: In 2009, Youngsteadt, Alvarez Baca, and Osborne found ants farming their hosts. Arboreal ants in Amazonia collected and planted specific host seeds. The obligate mutualism proved species-specific. The study maps a living seed exchange. The ants cultivate seeds in nutrient-rich nests.
plos-pone-0357735: Self-driving cars must guess where nearby vehicles will go next. This paper built a non-local multi-head spatiotemporal attention LSTM that predicts vehicle trajectories from their past paths. The architecture captures long-range interactions between cars, aiming for forecasts a driver — human or machine — can trust.
plos-pone-0358335: Fulminant myocarditis can kill a child within hours — and it looks like a stomach bug at first. This paper identified clinical characteristics and emergency-department warning indicators of the condition in children. The red flags give ER doctors a checklist for catching this heart emergency in time to save lives.
plos-pone-0358235: Melanoma tumors aren’t uniform — their neighborhoods matter. This paper mapped the spatial compartmentalization of melanoma cell states, revealing CAF-associated tumor cells with enhanced proliferative capacity. The geography of the tumor points to exactly where it grows fastest and where therapy should strike.
plos-pone-0342635: Heart muscle thickening in this mouse model coincides with hyaluronan buildup. This paper showed cardiomyocyte hypertrophy co-localizes with accumulation of hyaluronan in cMyBPC heterozygous mouse hearts. The co-localization hints at a disease mechanism linking structural proteins to the heart’s gel-like matrix.
plos-pone-0353935: Conspiracy believers who turn physically aggressive often carry deeper wounds than ideology alone. This longitudinal population-based study found they frequently faced various psycho-social problems across their lives. The life histories reframe a lazy stereotype — aggression here looks more like pain than politics.
plos-pone-0357035: Quantum secure direct communication protocols promise unbreakable messaging — but only if they survive cryptanalysis. This paper cryptanalyzed a controller-independent controlled bidirectional QSDC protocol, exposing its weaknesses. The attack ultimately strengthens quantum cryptography by revealing what to fix.
plos-pone-0354335: A simple wedge in the shoe might realign an arthritic knee — but does height matter? This paper studied the impact of insole wedge height on knee alignment, joint space width, and patient-reported outcomes in medial knee osteoarthritis. The dose-response findings help clinicians prescribe the right wedge, not just any wedge.
plos-pone-0355735: Sterilizing heat-sensitive equipment at room temperature is a long-standing challenge. This paper introduced nitric oxide gas as a novel sterilization modality — effective without heat. The room-temperature approach could transform how clinics sterilize delicate instruments.
plos-pone-0356235: Cassava — Africa’s staple — is slow and disease-prone to propagate by cuttings. This paper developed and evaluated a synthetic seed system for cassava propagation. The artificial seeds promise faster, cleaner multiplication of improved varieties — a potential revolution for food security.
plos-pone-0355935: Illinois residents mailing in ticks they find — community science at its best. This community-engaged passive tick surveillance highlighted the diversity of ticks and tick-borne pathogens across the state. The citizen-powered data reveal disease risks that professional surveillance alone would miss.
plos-pone-0355835: Heat kills — and in basin-trapped megacities the toll is amplified. This paper assessed temperature’s impact on mortality burden and economic losses in a basin-located mega-city. The quantified damages make the economic case for cooling interventions that save both lives and money.
plos-pone-0354635: Young breast cancer survivors face existential distress during rehabilitation — shaped by how they adapt psychologically. This paper analyzed the chain mediating psychosocial adaptation’s influence on that distress. The findings reveal intervention points where support can ease the deepest questions survivorship raises.
plos-pone-0351135: Clinicians can’t read every practice-changing trial — but LLMs can summarize them. Trial Files leverages large language models to distill practice-changing clinical trials for busy clinicians. The AI summaries promise to close the gap between published evidence and bedside practice.
plos-pone-0353835: ‘Another Me’ — a digital twin — might help people build real human relationships. This exploratory randomized controlled study investigated the technology’s role in supporting relationship development. The findings probe whether a virtual self can genuinely improve how we connect with actual others.
plos-pone-0355335: ECG signals are only useful if they’re clean — and quality varies. This paper developed a global-key region collaborative noise-aware method for ECG signal quality assessment. The quality scoring ensures cardiac AI trains on signals worth trusting — and clinicians aren’t misled by noise.
europmc-pmc2810335: Macrophages, the immune system's cleanup crew, change their behavior in artery disease. This 2010 paper studies macrophage plasticity in experimental atherosclerosis, showing these cells shift roles as plaques develop. The authors map how their functions evolve during disease. Understanding these shifts matters because macrophages drive both plaque growth and stability.
europmc-pmc2845135: Most tumor hunts chase rogue genes, but this 2010 paper calls the illness a fuel problem at root. The authors cast cancer as sick cell burners, not just bad code. Their flip dares the gene-first creed. The bold claim lit debate on whether fuel fixes might cure growths.
europmc-pmc2877735: Chemotherapy ravages the gut lining, and gut germs may worsen it. This 2010 review examines the role of intestinal microbiota in chemo-induced mouth and gut sores. The authors weigh how microbes shape the damage. Their overview suggests protecting gut flora could ease a dreaded side effect.
europmc-pmc2936535: Mutations lean toward A and T in bacteria, this 2010 paper argues. The authors gather evidence that mutation is universally biased toward AT across bacteria. Their finding reframes how genomes evolve. The work explains puzzling GC-content patterns. The bias shapes every bacterial genome over time.
europmc-pmc2948035: A crop spray's effects may echo down rat generations. This 2010 study finds the spray vinclozolin leaves marks on sperm DNA that grandpups inherit. The authors show the marks persist. Their work raised alarms about chemical legacies. Rule-makers cite it in hormone-chemical debates.
europmc-pmc2987835: Aphids inject spit weapons into plants, and this 2010 paper hunts them. The authors use gene screens to find candidate attack proteins from the green peach aphid. Their hunt reveals the arsenal. The work aids crop protection. Blocking these proteins could shield harvests.
europmc-pmc2993935: Resistant starch feeds gut germs differently by type. This 2010 human study finds starch types 2 and 4 shift gut germ mixes in different ways. The authors reveal the selective feeding. Their work informs prebiotic food design. Not all fiber feeds the same germs.
europmc-pmc3020935: Immune disease genes cluster in protein networks. This 2011 paper shows proteins from immune-disease regions touch each other in cells. The authors reveal the wiring. Their work suggests shared roots. One drug might treat several such diseases. The wiring map guides target hunting.
europmc-pmc3031535: Plants fight viruses with a slicer protein. This 2011 paper shows the AGO2 protein defends plants against viruses. The authors reveal the defender at work. Their work aids crop protection. The slicer chops viral RNA into bits. Breeders now boost this defense in crops.
europmc-pmc3072935: Guidelines gather dust unless usable. This 2011 paper offers a plain framework for making guidelines doctors will follow. The authors guide guideline writers. Their work shaped standards. Short, clear, and actionable wins, they find. The framework now anchors training courses. Hospitals audit against the framework.
europmc-pmc6510035: Pseudomonas aeruginosa ranks among the world's most dangerous drug-resistant germs, and much of its power comes from biofilms - slimy bacterial communities where antibiotics barely reach. This review explains how these films help the bacteria tolerate and resist treatment. Understanding the escape tricks is a key step toward drugs that can break through and save patients.
europmc-pmc6523135: Every animal cell contains a shifting scaffold of protein filaments - the cytoskeleton - that hauls cargo, divides the cell, and lets it crawl. This review tours the three filament systems and the dense web of crosslinks between them. Far from a static skeleton, the meshwork constantly rebuilds itself, and its failures underlie diseases from muscular dystrophy to cancer spread.
europmc-pmc6588935: Bladder tumors grow faster when an enzyme called METTL3 tags their RNA with m6A marks - specifically speeding the maturation of two cancer-promoting microRNAs, miR-221 and miR-222. This study nailed down the chain: more METTL3, more mature miR-221/222, more proliferation. Blocking the enzyme could brake bladder cancer's growth.
europmc-pmc6616535: Spotting malnutrition early saves lives - but which blood tests actually reflect nutritional status? This review evaluates laboratory markers: albumin and prealbumin, the traditional visceral proteins, and why the shorter-lived prealbumin better tracks rapid change. Clinicians get guidance on reading these numbers wisely.
europmc-pmc6678835: Garlic's bite comes with benefits: allicin, ajoene, and sulfur compounds with real bioactivity. This review catalogs garlic's chemical arsenal and the health effects studied so far - heart, immune, antimicrobial. The evidence backs the ancient remedy, with modern science still filling gaps.
europmc-pmc6708235: Predicting outcomes from thousands of genes demands regression that tolerates crowds. The glmnet software fits elastic-net models - accepting slightly biased estimates in exchange for far steadier predictions. This paper explains the statistical machinery, a workhorse behind modern biomarker hunting.
europmc-pmc6711235: Candida auris - the drug-resistant yeast haunting hospitals - was thought to have four family branches. Researchers in Iran found an isolate so genetically distant it may form a fifth clade, split by over 200,000 DNA differences. The discovery hints the pathogen's family tree is bigger than feared.
europmc-pmc6722135: The lung's housekeeping immune cells - interstitial macrophages - were long a blur. This study brings them into focus: non-classical monocytes and two distinct interstitial macrophage populations patrolling lung tissue. The single-cell census clarifies who does what in the lung's quiet corners.
europmc-pmc6769035: Natural killer cells assassinate tumors - but the tumor neighborhood starves them. This review examines NK cell metabolism in the tumor microenvironment: how the local chemistry saps their killing power. Feeding the assassins could restore immunotherapy's edge against solid tumors.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-35: This 2007 Government Accountability Office report looks at state and local fusion centers — the offices where police, federal agents, and analysts share intelligence about terrorism and crime. GAO found federal help was easing some of the centers' growing pains, from funding to data access. The report takes stock of an intelligence-sharing experiment that grew rapidly after 9/11 and asks whether Washington's support was keeping up.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1035: No Child Left Behind left schools guessing in 2007 — GAO's report says the Education Department owed clearer rules and a harder look at compliance traps. The findings walk the line between high standards and fair play for the schools graded under the landmark law.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-535: College sports were booming in 2007 — GAO's report tracks the trends in NCAA teams and players. The findings lay out who played what, where the growth ran, and what the money looked like. The report brings data to the eternal campus debate: big-time sports, big-time questions.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-735: Customs needed better data to catch fakes in 2007 — GAO's report says sharper analysis would help the border agency fight counterfeits. The findings press for smarter targeting of shipments. The report's logic: the knockoff trade leaves tracks, if anyone bothers to look.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-335: The Capitol's preservation purse got audited in 2007, and GAO's report grades the fund's financial statements for 2005 and 2004. The findings deliver the formal opinion for the record. The report shows the marble halls get the same ledger check as the war rooms.
openalex-w7206152235: Paperwork runs a police force, and in Alagoas the military police handle theirs through Brazil's electronic information system, the SEI. This paper studies how administrative processes are managed there and proposes a complementary management system to fix gaps the author found. It is a practical piece of public-administration engineering: part diagnosis of how the current digital workflow falls short, part blueprint for improving it.
openalex-w7172453835: Strong legs keep the elderly independent. This study followed 93 adults, median age 85, for a year to link function-focused training with leg strength. The authors measured the payoff of targeted exercise. A geriatrics study of training that keeps people on their feet.
openalex-w7214901235: Hard ceramics shatter, yet at tiny scales they can bend. This review sums up new work on bendability at room heat in oxide ceramics: nano poke tests and atom models. The authors tied inner structure to flex. A materials review of brittle stuff learning to give.
pmc-13505935: In this 2026 synthetic biology paper, scientists engineered gut bacteria to sense the host's stress hormones and respond with programmed actions. By wiring adrenaline-like signals into microbes, they created living sensors that can report or react when the body is stressed. The work points toward gut bacteria that act as diagnostic tools or even deliver treatments on cue.
pmc-13524335: A 2026 molecular biology paper identifying caveolin-1, a protein on human cells, as a key helper of a bacterial toxin made by Bacillus cereus. The toxin needs this host protein to punch holes in cells, and because the mechanism is shared across species, blocking it could weaken food-poisoning and infection-causing bacteria. The study pins down a possible target for future treatments.
pmc-13505635: A 2026 plant biology paper showing that DELLA proteins — growth regulators in plants — interact with HAC1 to control growth by tuning the activity of ERF2, a gene that represses growth. The study traces the transcriptional chain from DELLA to ERF2. Understanding this circuit matters for breeding crops with the right stature and timing.
pmc-13402935: A 2026 neuroscience paper on the behavioral effects of deleting the vesicular glutamate transporter 3 (VGLUT3) specifically in serotonin neurons of mice. The targeted deletion produced distinct phenotypic changes. The work dissects how glutamate co-release shapes serotonin system function.
pmc-13588635: This 2026 reply to Zhang and Lou argues that beta-blocker use after heart attack should be guided by indication, ejection fraction, and contemporary evidence — not habit. Scientific replies like this sharpen clinical debates. The authors make the case for selective, evidence-based prescribing.
pmc-13307635: In this 2026 paper, researchers assessed metabolism in human stem cell-derived cerebral organoids — lab-grown mini-brains — using HR-MAS NMR spectroscopy. Measuring metabolism in intact organoids validates them as brain models. The method advances organoid quality control.
pmc-13470535: In this 2026 paper, loss of pleasure (anhedonia) emerged as a sex-dependent, cross-species consequence of unpredictable signals to the perinatal brain. Early-life unpredictability scars reward systems differently by sex. The cross-species evidence strengthens the claim.
pmc-13431735: This 2026 review covered clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) in cardiovascular disease — gene-specific mechanisms and therapeutic implications. Aging blood clones drive heart risk. The review organizes the actionable biology.
pmc-13422835: A 2026 cluster randomized trial (Growing Up Without Violence) of a school-based intervention preventing adolescent sexual abuse and exploitation. The trial tested the program rigorously. The results inform prevention.
pmc-13530535: A 2026 conference poster on outcomes of arthroscopic treatment of 270–360 degree panlabral shoulder tears. The massive tears were treated minimally invasively. The poster reports the outcomes.
pmc-13518035: In this 2026 case report, severe tetanus followed a rooster-peck injury, requiring nasotracheal intubation. The barnyard wound turned life-threatening. The case is the warning.
pmc-13493535: A 2026 biomaterials review on silk fibroin-modified titanium implants for bone tissue engineering — structural basis, functionalization, and composite strategies. The silk-titanium hybrids were surveyed. The review organizes the field.
pmc-13478835: This 2026 paper assessed public-facing short videos on pediatric general anesthesia and child neurodevelopment — quality, misinformation, and implications for parent-centered research (the title is truncated). The videos' accuracy was graded. The misinformation findings matter.
pmc-13475735: In this 2026 paper, ZIP1 was identified as a critical DNA damage-responsive zinc transporter induced by bleomycin via the TNFα-NF-κB pathway. The zinc transporter's damage role was discovered. The induction mechanism is the finding.
pmc-13480435: This 2026 study linked lifestyle patterns to sleep disturbance among Black breast cancer survivors — results from the Women's Circle of Health Follow-Up Study. The survivors' sleep was tied to lifestyle. The patterns are the actionable insight.
pmc-13449035: In this 2026 paper, vitamin B3 (nicotinamide) supplementation was tested in primary and scleroderma-related Raynaud phenomenon. The vitamin's vascular effects were trialed. The supplementation is the intervention.
pmc-13437435: In this 2026 drug delivery paper, ultrasmall cyclodextrin-based nanogels were developed as drug delivery systems. The tiny gels carried drugs. The nanogels are the platform.
pmc-13520635: In this 2026 paper, differential roles of BRCA1 and BRCA2 in the DNA damage response were revealed by isogenic V79 mutant cell lines. The two genes' distinct jobs were separated. The revealing refines cancer biology.
pmc-13463835: This 2026 paper studied energy metabolism and nutritional condition of juvenile white sharks. The young predators' physiology was profiled. The condition data serve conservation.
pmc-13465135: In this 2026 paper, a highly sensitive electrochemical immunosensor based on core-shell SiO2-PEI@Ag nanoparticle nanocomposites was developed for MPA detection. The sensor's sensitivity was the achievement. The immunosensor serves diagnostics.
pmc-13434535: A 2026 South Korean secondary data analysis of risk and protective factors for intergenerational transmission of child maltreatment (the title is truncated). The abuse cycle's drivers were modeled. The factors guide prevention.
pmc-13524135: A 2026 first case report from India of Bordetella hinzii antenatal sepsis in a pregnant woman with sickle cell disease and intrauterine fetal demise. The rare pathogen's obstetric tragedy was documented. The case is the warning.
pmc-13521935: In this 2026 materials paper, high efficiency gold extraction was achieved by 2D metallic phase-transition metal dichalcogenides. The gold was pulled from solution. The extraction is the materials advance.
pmc-13463135: A 2026 paper with risk factor analysis and risk prediction model establishment for heterotopic ossification after open reduction and internal fixation of distal humeral fractures (the title is truncated). The abnormal bone growth was predicted. The model guides prevention.
pmc-13430735: This 2026 exploratory Ising model network analysis of cluster headache mapped conditional associations across symptoms, triggers, and pain localization. The headache's network was drawn. The mapping is the insight.
pmc-13421735: A 2026 study of AI for pediatric fracture detection — impact on diagnostic revisions and patient recall rates in a tertiary emergency setting. The AI's fracture reading was evaluated. The impact is the clinical evidence.
arxiv-2606-15935: Physicists ran an experiment sending light pulses through a special optical setup — a "quantum walk" of photons with intentional noise added. They watched for sudden, sharp changes in the light's behavior over time, a phenomenon called dynamical phase transitions. The paper reports what they observed and what it reveals about how quantum systems behave.
arxiv-2606-16235: Lay two odd films cheek by jowl and the seam can birth magnet tricks and flow traits owned by neither. This paper eyes one such seam — SrRuO3 on SrCuO2, whose grids don't match — and shows how the seam steers magnet pull and charge flow. For film-tech builders.
arxiv-2606-16335: Cancer care runs in acts — cut, zap, drug, watch — and sick folk lose the plot. This paper draws act-maps with the patient at heart, shaped by what sick folk must truly grasp. For med-pic crews and care teams who brief the ill.
arxiv-2606-16435: Generating audio and editing it are usually separate tasks. This paper unifies them: one model that both generates and edits audio, trained with joint condition modeling (handling many kinds of instructions together) and progressive training. It targets audio-AI researchers building flexible sound tools.
arxiv-2606-16535: Concept bottleneck models make decisions through human-understandable concepts — but only if their "symbol detection" is reliable. This paper assesses just that: how trustworthy is the model's claim that it sees a given concept? The work targets explainable-AI researchers who need concept-based models they can actually audit.
